title: U.S. House · Alabama's 6th Congressional District
area: Birmingham's suburbs and exurbs, including Shelby County, Tuscaloosa, and parts of central Alabama.

context.text: Incumbent Gary Palmer (R) defeated Case Dixon 85.7% to 14.3% in the August 11, 2026 Republican primary. Maurice Mercer defeated Ashtyn Kennedy, Keith Pilkington, and Jacob Bouma-Sims in the same-day Democratic primary. A new congressional map, signed after the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling, moved this district's primary from May 19 to August 11, 2026; the May 19 results were voided. Cook Political Report rated the district R+17 for 2026.

candidates.name: Gary Palmer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary, 85.7% to 14.3%, over Case Dixon.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Alabama's 6th Congressional District (since 2015)

summary.text: Gary Palmer is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Alabama's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2014. He chaired the House Republican Policy Committee from 2019 to 2025 and currently chairs the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee of the House Energy and Commerce Committee. Before Congress, he led the conservative think tank the Alabama Policy Institute.

background.text: Born in Haleyville, Alabama, in 1954; earned a bachelor's degree in operations management from the University of Alabama in 1977.
Led the Alabama Policy Institute, a conservative think tank, and served on Governor Robert Bentley's Alabama Commission on Improving State Government before his election to Congress.

priorities.text: As chair of the Energy and Commerce Environment Subcommittee, says securing the domestic supply chain of critical minerals, including refining and processing rare earth elements, is his top priority, citing reliance on China as a threat to economic and national security.
Says the ZOMBIE Act, which he sponsored and which passed the House in June 2026, requires federal agencies to hunt down improper payments to combat government waste.

positions.summary: Cosponsored and voted for H.R. 38, the Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act, and says restrictions on gun ownership are unconstitutional and harm law-abiding citizens.
positions.quote: As a staunch supporter of the 2nd Amendment, I am a proud cosponsor of and voted in favor of H.R. 38 today. This bill protects the constitutional right for law-abiding citizens to keep and bear arms and ensures that the right does not end when you cross a state line. Overreaching restrictions placed on gun ownership are not only unconstitutional, they inevitably harm law-abiding citizens and do little to dissuade the illegal use of firearms.

positions.summary: Applauded the 2015 reconciliation bill repealing major components of the Affordable Care Act, including the Medicaid expansion, premium tax credits, and individual and employer mandates, calling the ACA a failure.
positions.quote: Obamacare is a massive federal takeover of our health care industry that takes away choices from people and limits our freedom.

positions.summary: Voted to create a House select panel to investigate fetal tissue procurement and abortion providers' federal funding, saying Congress has an obligation to protect the unborn.
positions.quote: We have an obligation to protect the unborn and should take every opportunity to do so.

positions.summary: As chair of the Energy and Commerce Environment Subcommittee, describes himself as a skeptic of renewable energy and environmental regulations, calling the idea of meeting baseload power demand with renewables "insane," and prioritizes boosting domestic mineral and energy production over emissions rules.

record.text: Served as chairman of the House Republican Policy Committee from 2019 to 2025 (116th through 118th Congress); elected to the post in November 2018 and re-elected unopposed in November 2022. Kevin Hern succeeded him as chairman at the start of the 119th Congress in January 2025.
Chairs the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee of the House Energy and Commerce Committee and serves on its Energy and Environment subcommittees in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs; Government Operations subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.
Sponsored the ZOMBIE Act, which passed the House in June 2026 and requires federal agencies to identify and recover improper payments.

candidates.researchNotes: Palmer has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and no distinct 2026 campaign issues page was found; positions and priorities are drawn from press releases and news coverage linked from the issue pages on his official House site, which mix longstanding and recent statements (dated where the page itself gives a date).

candidates.name: Maurice Mercer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary with 64.2% of the vote over three other candidates.

summary.text: Maurice Mercer is a business account executive and former Pelham City Council member running as the Democratic nominee for Alabama's 6th Congressional District. He served three terms on the Pelham City Council, including as council president from 2020 to 2025, and was the council's first African American member.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Midfield High School and a bachelor's degree in business administration from Troy University in 2004.

Served on the Pelham City Council from 2012 to 2025, including as council president from 2020 to 2025; earned the Advanced Certified Municipal Officer designation and was named Public Servant of the Year three years in a row.

priorities.text: "Community First, Country Forward": says he has worked across party lines throughout his career and wants to restore civility to public office.
Education and workforce development, including support for expanded career and technical education, apprenticeships, and raising the federal minimum wage.
Healthcare access, including expanding affordable healthcare, protecting rural healthcare providers, and improving mental-health services.

positions.summary: Says he would like to see the federal minimum wage raised.
Says he is passionate about "healthcare for all" and supports expanding access to affordable healthcare and protecting rural providers.

record.text: Served three terms on the Pelham City Council (2012–2025), including as council president from 2020 to 2025.
